summary.en: Build a menu-driven linked-list phone book with text-file persistence and explicit ownership.
summary.bn: লিংকড লিস্ট আর টেক্সট ফাইল দিয়ে মেনু চালানো ফোন বুক বানাও।

notes: These programs use the C17 standard library.

sections.title: Connect the structures to a complete program
Write the command contract before the menu
Keep ownership through editing and sorting
Try editing and a file round-trip
Test the boundaries of the menu
Use a small application to test ownership

examples.title: Run the complete contact menu
examples.explanationHtml: Names are unique and compared case-sensitively. Sorting changes links, while phone numbers retain zeroes and the optional plus sign.

examples.title: Save, change and reload the contact list
examples.explanationHtml: Saving writes sorted rows to contacts.txt in the current folder. Loading rebuilds that order and restores the deleted contact. Use a scratch folder because W replaces this file.

practice.title: Exercise contact editing
practice.statementHtml: Implement the menu in example one. Read one command per line until Q or EOF; obey the 32-contact limit, unique case-sensitive names and bounded text rules in the lesson. Print the exact menu line and the matching added/rejected/no memory, lookup row/not found, deleted, sorted, contacts: list, saved/save failed, loaded/load failed or invalid command/invalid line responses.
hints: Keep list ownership in one head pointer.

practice.title: Round-trip a sorted phone book
practice.statementHtml: Using the same menu contract, support W and R with contacts.txt in the current folder. Preserve file order when loading. A failed load must leave existing contacts intact. Each sequence writes its file before reading it.

practice.title: Plan a safer save
practice.statementHtml: Why can fopen with mode w lose an earlier file even if saving reports failure? Describe a stronger save design.
hints: Saving and loading have different rollback guarantees.
practice.answerHtml: Opening in w mode truncates the previous file immediately. A later write or close failure can leave partial content. A stronger design writes a temporary file in the same directory, checks every write and close, then replaces the old file only after success. Platform durability needs additional filesystem support beyond these portable C17 examples.

quiz.prompt: Why store a phone number as text rather than int?
options: To preserve leading zeroes and an optional plus sign
To allow arithmetic sorting by phone
To avoid storing its length limit
To make every name unique
quiz.explanation: A phone number is an identifier rather than a quantity.

quiz.prompt: What must a failed phone-book load preserve?
options: Only the last parsed contact
The edited in-memory list
An empty head regardless of previous state
A partially loaded prefix
quiz.explanation: Build a temporary list and publish only after complete success.

quiz.prompt: Why is sorting by relinking useful for these contact nodes?
options: It makes insertion sort O(log n)
It eliminates every pointer update
Each contact retains its own name and phone fields
It changes names to numeric IDs
quiz.explanation: Node ownership remains clear while order changes.

quiz.prompt: Which limitation belongs to the demonstrated W command?
options: It cannot store leading zeroes
It cannot save an empty list
It guarantees crash-proof atomic replacement
Opening contacts.txt with w truncates an earlier file
quiz.explanation: Write and close errors are reported, but saving has no portable transactional replacement guarantee.

quiz.prompt: Which duplicate-name policy does the project enforce?
options: Reject a second exact case-sensitive name
Always append it
Silently change the old phone
Ignore case without conversion
quiz.explanation: The menu uses strcmp equality and treats names as unique keys.

quiz.prompt: How many list nodes remain after deleting the only contact?
quiz.explanation: Minus one is the indexed illustration of an empty head.

quiz.prompt: Which ASCII phone character survives when text begins with two zeroes?
quiz.explanation: Text keeps both leading zero digits.

quiz.prompt: What order does front insertion create for contact IDs one then two?
quiz.explanation: The most recently added node becomes the head before sorting.

keyPoints.en: A contact owns bounded name and phone text plus a next link.
keyPoints.bn: কনট্যাক্ট নোডে সীমিত নাম, ফোনের টেক্সট আর পরের নোডের লিংক থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Phone numbers remain strings so leading zeroes survive.
keyPoints.bn: ফোন নম্বর স্ট্রিংয়ে রাখলে শুরুর শূন্য হারায় না।

keyPoints.en: Sort contacts by relinking nodes instead of copying identities.
keyPoints.bn: নোডের লিংক বদলে কনট্যাক্ট সাজাও, পরিচয় কপি করে নয়।

keyPoints.en: Load into a temporary list before replacing current contacts.
keyPoints.bn: বর্তমান কনট্যাক্ট বদলানোর আগে অস্থায়ী লিস্টে ফাইল লোড করো।

keyPoints.en: Release every contact when the menu ends.
keyPoints.bn: মেনুর কাজ শেষ হলে সব কনট্যাক্টের মেমরি ফ্রি করো।

examQuestions.question: Design the phone book ownership rule and give costs for add, search, delete and sort.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The head owns every reachable node exactly once. Each node owns its name and phone arrays. Unique-name add scans O(n), search and delete are O(n), and insertion sort is O(n squared). Link edits after finding a position take O(1) time. The list uses O(n) records; sorting needs O(1) auxiliary pointers.

examQuestions.question: Explain how a failed file load can avoid destroying edited contacts.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Open the file, parse bounded rows into a temporary list, reject malformed rows, duplicates, excess contacts and allocation failures, and close the file. On failure release only the temporary list. On complete success restore file order, release the previous list, and publish the new head.
